title: Implement graceful jit-server process shutdown
description:
Shared SSE cancellation plus `axum-server`'s deadline-aware handle guarantees clean exit even when an ordinary connection cannot finish voluntarily.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Add `axum-server` 0.8 and `tokio-util`; define one application constant `GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT = Duration::from_secs(5)`. One `CancellationToken` is cloned into AppState/router/SSE, and one `axum_server::Handle` owns listener/connection shutdown. Registered Ctrl-C or Unix terminate errors propagate.
- [hard] REQ-02: On signal, cancel the token first so `sse::change_stream` reaches EOF and its 15-second keepalive stops, then call `handle.graceful_shutdown(Some(GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT))`. The server stops acceptance, allows ordinary connections at most five seconds, force-closes/aborts survivors at the deadline, and its future returns `Ok`; logs include signal, deadline, connection count before/at expiry, forced-close path, and clean completion.
- [hard] REQ-03: A Unix real-process test opens `/api/events/stream`, observes initial/keepalive connection, and starts a deliberately non-completing ordinary response/body or stalled connection. After SIGTERM it requires SSE EOF promptly, the ordinary connection forcibly closed at the five-second deadline, socket closure and process exit 0 in strictly less than ten seconds—never signal death, test-side kill, or 137.
- [hard] REQ-04: Fixtures cover multiple SSE plus completing and non-completing ordinary requests, connection-count/deadline logs, no child, valid repository and immediate restart. Cross-platform tests cover token/Ctrl-C/handle behavior without Unix-only APIs.
- [hard] REQ-05: The new `axum-server`/`tokio-util` versions are pinned by Cargo.lock, compile on declared MSRV, and pass `cargo audit -D warnings`; no advisory allowlist is added.

## Notes

Blast radius: `crates/server/src/main.rs`, `routes.rs`/`AppState`, `sse.rs`, optional shutdown/test-only routes or modules, `crates/server/tests/`, `crates/server/Cargo.toml`, workspace `Cargo.lock`, and Rust security-audit evidence; domain and storage semantics are unchanged.
